sourceEvidence.label: LedgerBridge internal upload, Connector and runner boundary

assessment.summary: The route has a trusted-principal seam but no provider, and individual Connector validation but no deployment-owned manifest. Two separate admission boundaries should be designed before enablement.

nonNegotiables: Keep LEDGERBRIDGE_ENABLE_INTERNAL_UPLOAD false by default and reject it in production.
Do not register a real Connector or ingest evidence during design.
Keep runner network-disabled, read-only, low-privilege and credential-free.
Do not place credentials or signing keys in the repository.
assumptions: No identity provider, signing service or latency budget has been selected.
The current synchronous route is internal/test-only until a separate exposure decision.
API-to-runner socket composition is unresolved and must be explicitly reviewed.

opportunities.title: Trusted principal admission for evidence upload
opportunities.summary: Give the route an owned authentication and capability decision before any body bytes are consumed.
opportunities.diagnosis: The route checks a syntactically safe request.state value, but no provider proves who produced it or whether the caller has evidence:write authority.

evidence.claim: get_authenticated_principal reads request.state.authenticated_principal; no verifier, issuer, audience, expiry or scope policy is present.
The approved upload contract requires server-derived actor authentication before body read and keeps provider integration as a separate gate.
Without an owned producer, a future adapter could copy an attacker-controlled identity into request state while passing text validation.

desiredInvariants: Authentication and evidence:write authorization complete before body read or staging.
Only a verifier-owned typed principal can supply the audit actor.
Invalid, expired, wrong-audience or insufficient-scope credentials fail closed without token leakage.

options.title: Trusted internal gateway/middleware
options.summary: Use loopback or mTLS gateway policy to install a typed principal in request state.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The state seam gets an owned gateway/middleware producer.
Authentication remains before body read and actor remains server-derived.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes raw-header substitution for the internal transport, but proxy policy remains critical.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Bypass-gateway and certificate-mapping tests must fail before body read.

tradeoffs.assessment: Avoids per-request JWKS lookup; a local middleware path is bounded.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure warm request latency with gateway and direct-loopback profiles.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only a bounded typed principal and policy generation are retained.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Check peak RSS with concurrent rejected and accepted requests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fail-closed gateway absence prevents unauthenticated import, but gateway availability gates uploads.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise gateway outage, direct access and certificate expiry.

tradeoffs.assessment: Certificate/SAN mapping and proxy policy need runbooks and telemetry.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review rotation, alerting and incident procedures in a disposable profile.

tradeoffs.assessment: Preserves the route/importer API and can be introduced without production enablement.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run dependency-override tests and a loopback/mTLS integration profile.

residualRisks: A bypassed or misconfigured gateway can still produce a valid-looking state value.
Not suitable as a remote multi-client identity contract.

workPackages: Define typed principal and capability policy
acceptanceCriteria: Every auth failure occurs before body read and staging
No raw actor header is accepted
Production flag remains false and forced off
migrationNotes: Keep the provider as a dependency seam so OIDC can replace it later.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Keep the route disabled and revert the middleware binding; never fall back to client headers.

options.title: OIDC/JWT verifier in the API boundary
options.summary: Verify issuer, audience, signature, time claims and evidence:write scope before route body read.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The dependency becomes a verifier-backed policy rather than a state convention.
Provider settings, key cache and failure policy become explicit configuration.

tradeoffs.assessment: Provides portable proof and claim-level authorization, with verifier and key-policy risk made explicit.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use forged, expired, wrong-audience, wrong-key and insufficient-scope tokens.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds token parsing and bounded cached-key verification to each request.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure cold/warm p50 and p95 auth latency under concurrent upload attempts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires a bounded JWKS cache and claim objects.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure RSS with key rotation and cache-size limits.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fail-closed JWKS outages protect admission but can deny legitimate internal uploads.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define and test key-cache outage and revocation windows.

tradeoffs.assessment: Issuer, audience, clock, key rotation and redacted auth telemetry require new runbooks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a provider rotation and outage rehearsal without real tokens.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires provider selection and policy coordination before it can replace the internal seam.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Shadow-verify in test before making the policy enforcing.

residualRisks: Verifier implementation and key-management failures become a privileged choke point.
Provider outage policy may trade availability for fail-closed security.

workPackages: Add redacted auth telemetry and outage runbook
acceptanceCriteria: All invalid token classes fail before body read
No token or raw claim appears in logs or responses
migrationNotes: Use only after a remote or multi-client exposure decision.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the provider-backed route and keep the production flag closed; do not accept unsigned headers.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the trusted internal boundary while the route is loopback/internal and off by default; select the OIDC/JWT option before remote or multi-client exposure.

opportunities.title: Reviewable Connector manifest governance
opportunities.summary: Make the enabled Connector set, source-system ownership, code identity and runner capability boundary deployment-owned.
opportunities.diagnosis: Individual Connector objects are validated, but API, worker and runner have no shared manifest or generation agreement and the runner starts empty.

evidence.claim: get_internal_connectors returns an empty sequence, so the route has no production Connector registry.
validate_connector enforces object identity and production runner mode but does not select or attest implementation factories.
ConnectorSupervisor starts with an empty mapping unless tests inject connectors; its no-network boundary is not a manifest authority.
API/worker/runner can drift because the API does not mount connector-socket and no composition loader compares a manifest generation.

desiredInvariants: Requests never select Connector identity or source_system.
Every enabled entry has unique identity, canonical source-system ownership, allowlisted factory, protocol and bounded capability policy.
API, worker and runner load the same immutable generation/digest or fail closed.
Production entries are runner-only and cannot grant network, database, artifact or OAuth authority.

options.title: Static built-in manifest
options.summary: Use a code-owned tuple and allowlisted factory map validated at startup.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Retains object-level validation while centralizing construction.
Adds a shared composition root instead of empty per-process defaults.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes request-selected factories, but code/image drift remains a residual risk.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare startup manifest digest and image revision across API, worker and runner.

tradeoffs.assessment: Construction is startup-only and request detection keeps the existing path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark startup and detection for one and many synthetic entries.

tradeoffs.assessment: Retains the existing connector objects and a small tuple.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure process RSS across registry sizes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Invalid sets fail closed at startup instead of partially enabling callers.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject duplicate, missing-source and factory-construction failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Uses code review and image rollout without a new signing service.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify digest telemetry and rollback to empty registry.

tradeoffs.assessment: Minimal change for synthetic fixtures and preserves the Connector protocol.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run current importer and runner suites with a static test manifest.

residualRisks: Manifest identity is implicit in the code/image and can drift between compositions.
No independent attestation of the factory implementation.

workPackages: Define factory allowlist and shared loader
Validate source registry and runner mode
migrationNotes: Use for synthetic/test connectors while signature infrastructure is absent.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Deploy the empty static manifest or revert the composition revision.

options.title: Signed declarative manifest plus runner
options.summary: Verify a signed immutable manifest, map only allowlisted factories, and require generation agreement across API, worker and runner.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Signature is an enablement control; object contract validation remains a second defense.
Runner registry becomes an explicit, verified generation instead of an empty implicit map.
Manifest capabilities are cross-checked against the no-network/read-only Compose boundary.

tradeoffs.assessment: Makes enablement, code identity and generation agreement reviewable while preserving runner isolation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test signature, factory, source registry, image digest, capability and cross-process mismatch failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds bounded startup verification and manifest parsing; request path remains importer/socket bounded.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure startup and request p95 before/after with one and many entries.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds manifest and verification-key material to each consumer.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure RSS and cache limits in API, worker and runner images.

tradeoffs.assessment: Mixed or invalid generations fail closed instead of silently running a different parser.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Replay partial rollout, missing-key and rollback scenarios.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires signing, key rotation, digest telemetry, generation rollout and incident runbooks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise a disposable signing/verification workflow with no production key.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires schema/factory pipeline and an explicit API-to-runner socket or async handoff decision.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run Linux Compose tests for both composition choices before real enablement.

residualRisks: A compromised signing process can authorize a malicious allowlisted factory.
A valid manifest cannot compensate for an overprivileged Compose mount or missing API socket decision.

workPackages: Resolve synchronous socket versus worker async composition
acceptanceCriteria: All consumers report the same manifest digest
Runner capabilities never exceed Compose authority
migrationNotes: Start with an empty signed generation and synthetic test fixtures; add real source-system rows only after separate approval.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Select the previous signed generation or empty manifest and restart all consumers; keep the route flag closed during rollback.

opportunities.recommendation: Use a static manifest only for synthetic/test fixtures; require the signed declarative runner manifest for any real Connector or production path.

openQuestions: Which internal gateway or OIDC issuer is approved for Hermes?
Will synchronous API execution mount the runner socket, or will Connector execution move to the worker?
Where will manifest signing and verification keys be managed and rotated?
Which owner approves source-system registration, factory IDs and parser versions?
